subject: Urgent: priority lanes & surge scheduling for CatalystAI launch
messages:
From: Ava Torres <ava.t@catalyst.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: James Li <james.li@catalyst.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prod launch next week — need priority lanes and surge allocation

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We have a hard production launch date for our recommendation feature on 2028-03-22 and the engineering team hit a performance sweet spot using the gen-2-large model on dedicated infra. We need a short, predictable window of elevated capacity (approx 8 A100-80GB equivalent GPUs) for the first 72 hours of launch with strict latency SLOs.

Can Redwood provide:
- A temporary priority lane (traffic routed ahead of non-priority bursts) for CatalystAI for 03/22–03/25
- Guaranteed reserved burst capacity or a tranche we can buy for those dates
- An SOW and pricing for the surge / priority handling and rollback conditions

Procurement is standing by to sign quickly if we can get a clear capacity plan and SOW. Attaching our internal cutover plan for context (small attachment).

Appreciate a quick read — this is critical to the launch.

Best,
Ava Torres
Head of Platform Engineering
CatalystAI
[Attachment: catalyst_cutover_notes.txt (txt)]

----
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Torres <ava.t@catalyst.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod launch next week — need priority lanes and surge allocation

Hi Ava — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the launch.

Short answer: we can support a 72-hour elevated window, but there are tradeoffs to be explicit about so expectations line up:
- We can create a priority lane that routes your traffic to a reserved tranche; that prevents preemption but requires pinning capacity for the window.
- Alternatively, we can provide a burst reservation with preemptible lower-priority background workloads reclaimed; this is cheaper but has a small risk if global capacity is constrained.

We need to confirm:
1) exact GPU equivalence and instance types (you mentioned A100-80GB equivalence — can you confirm vCPU/memory needs for sidecar components?)
2) acceptable latency P50/P95 targets and max token/sec baseline during peak
3) whether you want automatic rollback to hosted shared model if capacity issues occur

I'm looping in Ben (infrastructure) and Lauren (revenue ops) to propose the concrete tranche and pricing. Marcus, can you weigh in on feasibility for the weekend window and any blackout dates?

Jonas
Director, Sales (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference

----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ava Torres <ava.t@catalyst.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 12:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod launch next week — need priority lanes and surge allocation

Ava / team — internal ops note: we have a planned maintenance window on 03/23 for a subset of edge racks in us-west which reduces available burst headroom by ~2 A100 equivalents between 02:00–06:00 PT. That maintenance was scheduled to reduce failure rates; pushing it would be non-trivial but possible with +48h notice.

Proposed options (fast):
A) Reserve a 8-GPU tranche for 03/22 00:00–03/25 23:59 PT and route Catalyst traffic to that tranche (zero preemption). Price = reserved tranche daily rate * 3 + one-time priority lane config.
B) Provide a 10-GPU burst reservation with preemption protection during peak windows using warm standby instances; cheaper but we cannot guarantee zero preemption if another reserved tranche is active.
C) Hybrid: reserve 6 guaranteed GPUs + 2 burst-capacity GPUs and implement prefix caching to reduce token throughput needs.

I'll attach a quick capacity schedule and a micro SLO matrix. Lauren: can you prepare provisional SOW language and approved discount band for reserved tranche?

[Attachment: capacity_plan_catalyst_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

—Ben
Sr. Infra Ops, Redwood Inference

----
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Torres <ava.t@catalyst.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, James Li <james.li@catalyst.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Mar 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod launch next week — need priority lanes and surge allocation

Ava / James — thanks, I summarized the practical recommendation below so procurement can move:
- Option C (Hybrid) is my recommendation: reserve 6 guaranteed GPUs (A100-80GB equiv) + 2 burst GPUs for three days. This balances cost and risk given the maintenance on 03/23.
- We'll configure a priority routing policy for Catalyst traffic to the tranche and enable prefix cache for top-50 routes to reduce token load.
- SLA: we can commit to P95 latency target of 450ms for the reserved tranche. We will include an automatic fallback to a lighter-weight model hosted path if the tranche becomes unavailable; that fallback will be tagged in the SOW and must be exercised manually per your rollback runbook.

Lauren — can you confirm pricing and attach SOW? Neha — please approve any one-time engineering configuration credits (we typically offer a one-off launch credit for customers in this tier). Marcus / Ben — confirm the maintenance deferral or whether we should plan around the 03/23 02:00–06:00 PT window.

Jonas

----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ava Torres <ava.t@catalyst.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Procurement CatalystAI <procurement@catalyst.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod launch next week — need priority lanes & surge allocation (SOW attached)

Hi Ava & team — we reviewed and can proceed with the hybrid approach. Attached is the SOW and a one-page runbook for the 72-hour launch window. Key points:
- Reserved tranche: 6 A100-80GB equiv GPUs for 03/22 00:00 PT – 03/25 23:59 PT
- Burst tranche: up to 2 GPUs on warm standby; preemption exceptions documented in SOW
- One-time engineering configuration credit applied (20% of first-week tranche cost)
- DocuSign link for SOW: https://www.docusign.net/signature/SOW-CatalystAI

Procurement: please confirm payment terms and sign; we’ll schedule a short kickoff with infra on Monday 03/20 to cache top routes and run a smoke test.

Thanks — Neha Kapoor
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOW_CatalystAI_v2.pdf (pdf)]
